stem: Which concept describes the mechanism that mediates every access of subjects to objects and cannot be bypassed?

options.rationale: The reference monitor is the abstract mechanism that mediates all subject-object access; it must be non-bypassable, tamper-proof, and verifiable.
A firewall filters network traffic; it does not mediate all subject-object access within a system.
A rainbow table is a password-cracking tool, unrelated to access mediation.
A hash provides integrity fingerprints, not subject-object access mediation.

stem: Which set of properties MOST correctly describes the requirements of a reference monitor?

options.text: Tamper-proof, always invoked, and verifiable (small enough to analyze)
options.rationale: A reference monitor must be tamper-proof, always invoked (non-bypassable), and small/simple enough to be verified.
These are not the defining properties of a reference monitor.
This contradicts the requirements; it must be always invoked and verifiable/simple, not optional or complex.
These attributes are irrelevant to and inconsistent with reference-monitor requirements.

stem: How do the reference monitor and the security kernel MOST accurately relate?

options.text: The security kernel is the concrete implementation of the abstract reference monitor concept
options.rationale: The reference monitor is the concept; the security kernel (hardware/software/firmware) implements it.
They are directly related — one implements the other.

options.text: The reference monitor implements the security kernel
options.rationale: This reverses the relationship; the kernel implements the reference monitor concept.
Neither is an encryption algorithm; they are access-mediation concepts/components.

stem: The Trusted Computing Base (TCB) is MOST accurately defined as which of the following?

options.text: The totality of protection mechanisms that together enforce the security policy
options.rationale: The TCB is the sum of all hardware, software, and firmware components responsible for enforcing security policy.
The TCB is far broader than one application; it is the collection of all trusted protection components.
A browser is typically untrusted application code, not the TCB.
A business database is data, not the system's protection mechanisms.

stem: An exploited browser process is unable to read a banking app's memory on the same machine. Which capability MOST directly provides this protection?

options.text: Memory protection / process isolation (separate address spaces)
options.rationale: The OS gives each process an isolated address space, so one process cannot read or corrupt another's memory.
Network credentials do not isolate process memory.
Display hardware has no effect on memory isolation.
Storage size does not provide inter-process memory isolation.

stem: In a protection-ring architecture, which ring is MOST privileged?

options.rationale: Ring 0 is the most privileged level, running the kernel; higher-numbered rings are less privileged.
Ring 3 is typically the least privileged, running user applications.
Higher ring numbers mean less privilege, not more.
The ring model exists precisely to differentiate privilege levels.

stem: A laptop uses a hardware chip to securely store its full-disk-encryption key and verify boot integrity. This chip is MOST accurately called what?

options.rationale: A TPM provides hardware-based secure key storage and integrity/measured-boot functions, commonly protecting FDE keys.
A NIC handles network connectivity, not key storage or boot integrity.
A GPU accelerates graphics/compute, not cryptographic key storage.
A PSU provides power, unrelated to key storage.

stem: To prevent injected code from executing in memory regions meant only for data, which system capability is BEST?

options.text: Data Execution Prevention (DEP/NX) marking data pages non-executable
options.rationale: DEP/NX marks data memory as non-executable, blocking a common code-injection exploitation technique.

options.text: A louder system beep on errors
options.rationale: Audible alerts do not prevent code execution in data memory.
Disabling the firewall weakens security and does not address in-memory code execution.
Display settings are irrelevant to memory execution controls.

stem: A system randomizes the memory addresses used by processes each time they run, making it harder for exploits to predict where to jump. This capability is MOST accurately called what?

options.rationale: ASLR randomizes memory layout so attackers cannot reliably predict addresses, hindering memory-corruption exploits.
Round-robin scheduling allocates CPU time; it does not randomize memory layout.
Defragmentation reorganizes disk storage, not process memory layout.
Load balancing distributes traffic across servers, unrelated to memory randomization.

stem: Running each risky workload in its own isolated virtual machine MOST directly provides which security benefit?

options.text: Isolation, so a compromise in one VM is contained from others
options.rationale: Virtualization isolates workloads so that compromise of one guest is contained and does not directly affect others (subject to hypervisor security).
Isolation reduces blast radius but does not make workloads immune to attack.

options.text: Elimination of the need for patching
options.rationale: VMs still require patching; isolation does not remove that need.
Virtualization provides isolation, not automatic data encryption.

stem: An access-control mechanism can sometimes be bypassed under certain conditions. Which reference-monitor property does this MOST directly violate?

options.rationale: If access can bypass the mechanism, it is not 'always invoked,' violating a core reference-monitor requirement.
UI aesthetics are not a reference-monitor property.
Hosting location is not a reference-monitor property.
Reference monitors should be small/simple; largeness is not a required property and is not what a bypass violates.

stem: Why is keeping the Trusted Computing Base as small as possible MOST desirable?

options.text: A smaller TCB is easier to verify and has less code that could contain exploitable flaws
options.rationale: Minimizing the TCB reduces the amount of trusted code, making it more analyzable and less likely to harbor vulnerabilities.

options.text: A smaller TCB automatically encrypts all data
options.rationale: TCB size is unrelated to automatic encryption.

options.text: A larger TCB is always more secure
options.rationale: A larger trusted base means more code to trust and more potential flaws — less desirable.

options.text: TCB size has no security relevance
options.rationale: TCB size directly affects verifiability and attack surface of the trusted core.

stem: A compromised user-mode application cannot directly execute privileged kernel instructions. Which capability MOST directly enforces this separation?

options.text: Processor privilege levels (protection rings) separating kernel and user mode
options.rationale: Privilege levels/rings keep kernel operations (ring 0) separate from user-mode code, preventing direct privileged execution by user apps.
Screensavers do not enforce kernel/user separation.
Spam filtering is unrelated to CPU privilege separation.
Display size has no role in privilege separation.

stem: A laptop's TPM refuses to release the disk-encryption key after boot files are tampered with. This behavior MOST directly demonstrates which capability?

options.text: Boot integrity measurement (measured/secure boot) tied to key release
options.rationale: A TPM can measure boot components and release keys only if integrity checks pass, so tampering prevents key release.
Performance is unrelated to integrity-gated key release.
Compression is unrelated to boot integrity measurement.
Load balancing is unrelated to TPM boot integrity functions.

stem: Which statement best defines the reference monitor?

options.text: An abstract machine that mediates all access between subjects and objects
options.rationale: The reference monitor is the abstract concept mediating every subject-object access according to the security policy.

options.text: A tool that cracks password hashes
options.rationale: That describes a cracking tool, not the reference monitor.
Backup scheduling is unrelated to access mediation.
The reference monitor is a logical access-mediation concept, not a physical lock.

stem: What is the PRIMARY security benefit of process isolation provided by the operating system?

options.text: One process cannot read or corrupt another process's memory
options.rationale: Process isolation confines each process to its own memory, preventing cross-process reading or tampering.
Isolation is a protection mechanism, not primarily a performance feature.
Isolation does not perform backups.
Process isolation does not encrypt network traffic.

stem: When analyzing a system's security, which component would MOST likely be considered part of the TCB?

options.text: The operating system kernel enforcing access control
options.rationale: The kernel enforcing security policy is a core part of the trusted computing base.
A user application like a game is untrusted code, outside the TCB.
A spreadsheet is data/application content, not a trusted protection mechanism.
An email is not a system protection component.

stem: Why is storing an encryption key in a TPM MOST preferable to storing it in a plaintext OS file?

options.text: The TPM keeps the key in tamper-resistant hardware, not exposed in the file system
options.rationale: A TPM protects keys in hardware, unlike a plaintext file that any file-system access could read.

options.text: The TPM makes the key run faster
options.rationale: The benefit is protection, not key speed.

options.text: A plaintext file is more secure than a TPM
options.rationale: A plaintext key file is far less secure than TPM-protected storage.

options.text: The TPM publishes the key for transparency
options.rationale: A TPM protects keys from exposure; it does not publish them.

stem: To harden endpoints against memory-corruption exploits, which combination of system capabilities is BEST?

options.rationale: Combining address-space randomization (ASLR) with non-executable data memory (DEP/NX) raises the difficulty of memory-corruption exploitation.

options.text: Disabling ASLR and DEP for compatibility
options.rationale: Disabling these protections makes exploitation easier, the opposite of hardening.
Wallpaper has no security effect on memory exploits.
Removing memory protection removes a key defense.

stem: Which of the following is LEAST relevant as a built-in security capability of an information system?

options.text: The desktop background image chosen by the user
options.rationale: The wallpaper image is cosmetic and provides no security capability, making it least relevant.
Process isolation is a core security capability.
Privilege separation via rings is a fundamental security capability.

options.text: A TPM for key storage and boot integrity
options.rationale: A TPM provides real hardware security capabilities.
